title: Find cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing that still depends on EWS
problem: Organization Relationships and Sharing Policies that share Free/Busy, MailTips or calendars with other Microsoft 365 tenants depend on EWS, which Exchange Online is switching off. Before you move them to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy you need an inventory of what exists, who it applies to and which partners are cloud-hosted.
steps: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell with an account that has the Organization Management role. Set `$FormatEnumerationLimit = -1` so long domain lists are not truncated.

List enabled Organization Relationships: `Get-OrganizationRelationship | Where-Object { $_.Enabled } | Format-List Name, DomainNames, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScope, TargetSharingEpr, TargetAutodiscoverEpr, TargetApplicationUri`.

For each relationship with Free/Busy or MailTips enabled, decide whether the partner is in Microsoft 365: Microsoft's guide says a TargetSharingEpr or TargetAutodiscoverEpr containing outlook.com, office365.com or office365.us indicates a Microsoft 365-hosted partner; other values may indicate on-premises Exchange.

List Availability Address Spaces with `Get-AvailabilityAddressSpace | Format-List ForestName, AccessMethod, TargetAutodiscoverEpr, TargetServiceEpr, TargetTenantId`. Microsoft notes these do not depend on EWS for Microsoft 365 partners, so they are optional to migrate.

List Sharing Policies with `Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Enabled, Domains, Default` and note every domain rule with CalendarSharingFreeBusySimple, Detail or Reviewer, plus any Anonymous rule (published calendars).

Count which mailboxes each policy actually applies to: `Get-EXOMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -RecipientTypeDetails UserMailbox,SharedMailbox -Properties SharingPolicy | Group-Object SharingPolicy | Select-Object Name, Count`.
Record each in-scope partner's Entra tenant ID (ask their admin) and whether they will also migrate — the new policy is inbound-only, so two-way sharing needs a policy in both tenants.

Hand the inventory to the migration: Free/Busy and MailTips can move to Cross-Tenant Access Policy now; keep calendar-sharing policies until XTAP calendar sharing has reached your tenant (Microsoft's worldwide target is 23 November 2026).
pitfalls: Removing a Sharing Policy that still serves an on-premises or hybrid partner: Cross-Tenant Access Policy only covers organizations hosted in Microsoft 365, so that partner loses sharing.
Reusing one Organization Relationship for other features such as cross-tenant mailbox migration. Microsoft says to move those to a separate relationship before migrating Free/Busy or MailTips.
Forgetting the Anonymous rule in a Sharing Policy: published calendar URLs are a separate scenario from partner sharing.
Assuming the partner side is done because yours is: each tenant controls inbound access only.
done_when: Every enabled Organization Relationship, Availability Address Space and Sharing Policy is listed with partner domain, hosting (Microsoft 365 or on-premises), access level, scope and mailbox count.
Each Microsoft 365-hosted partner has a recorded tenant ID and an agreed migration owner on both sides.
On-premises and hybrid partners are flagged as out of scope for Cross-Tenant Access Policy.

troubleshooting.symptom: DomainNames or Domains output ends in '...'
troubleshooting.fix: Run `$FormatEnumerationLimit = -1` in the session before the Format-List commands.

troubleshooting.symptom: Partners report that your free/busy disappeared before you migrated
troubleshooting.cause: EWS is being gradually disabled in Exchange Online
troubleshooting.fix: Check the EWS deprecation guidance; Microsoft documents keeping EWS enabled (EWSEnabled) as a bridge until the final shutdown on 1 April 2027.
